definition: Basic personality refers to the broad underlying traits used to describe a person’s characteristic style of thinking, feeling, and behaving. In the source material, this is framed through the Big Five model: neuroticism, extroversion, conscientiousness, agreeableness, and openness.

reasons: Unsupported substantive claim: the packet does not define “basic personality” as broad underlying traits describing characteristic style of thinking, feeling, and behaving.

Partially supported: the packet mentions the Big Five model and lists the five traits (neuroticism, extroversion, conscientiousness, agreeableness, openness) and discusses personality traits/self-perception in relation to stress/anxiety/depression, but it does not support the specific wording or framing of the definition as a general meaning of the term “basic personality.”

The definition adds an unsupported gloss that basic personality means broad underlying traits describing a person’s characteristic style of thinking, feeling, and behaving; the packet only says the Big Five model embraces five basic personality traits.
The packet supports the Big Five list, but not the broader definitional framing or the implication that this is the meaning of the term rather than a model mentioned in the source.
